name: client-2026-exp-gain-u64
summary: 2026 client: NC_BAT_EXPGAIN (0x240B) is read as {u32 low, u16 handle, u32 high} - the EXP bar adds the u64 and "Obtained %s Exp." prints the full 64-bit amount.
status: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-25 by the client plugin client/plugins/exp64 (hooks/, no exe bytes changed) - DO NOT APPLY. v1 crashed the live client (unrelocated absolute address in its cave; the 2026 exe is ASLR-loaded); v2 (no absolute address) was built but never shipped. Kept as the record of the handler's layout.
why: 0x240B: case 0x58F6A7 news a 0x18-byte object and constructs it with the payload pointer (ctor 0x73F050):
0073F0AF  8B 01              mov  eax, [ecx]              ; payload u32 exp
0073F0B4  0F B7 41 04        movzx eax, word [ecx+4]      ; handle -> +0x14 and +8
The queued object's handler 0x73F0E0 (vtable 0xB4B5B4 slot 0):
0073F113  B9 08 BB C1 00     mov  ecx, 0xC1BB08
0073F11D  8B 43 10 85 C0     mov eax,[ebx+0x10] / test    ; 0 EXP: no line
0073F128  6A 00              push 0                       ; HIGH dword of the amount
0073F12A  50                 push eax                     ; low dword
0073F12B  8D 45 D8           lea  eax, [ebp-0x28]
0073F12E  50                 push eax
0073F12F  E8 ..              call 0x796200                ; localised number of a SIGNED 64-bit value
The client's EXP total (+0x192/+0x196) and its number formatter (0x796200 -> 0x796710: args buf, low, high) are
already 64-bit; only the packet read and the two pushes of 0 cut it to 32. The zone recipe exp-gain-u64 sends
{low, handle, high}, so: the object grows to 0x20, the ctor copies the high dword (payload +6) to +0x18, and the
handler adds low/high with add/adc, skips the line when both are 0, and passes high to the formatter. A negative
amount (sign-extended by the zone) adds and prints as negative, which the stock 32-bit add could not.
REQUIRES a server that sends the 12-byte 0x240B (our zones with exp-gain-u64): against a stock 6-byte server the
high dword would be read from past the payload.
v2 (2026-09-25): Fiesta.exe is DYNAMICBASE and Windows relocates it (live crash base 0xD70000). A cave must not hold
an absolute address: v1's `mov ecx, 0xC1BB08` was never relocated and the add at +8 faulted (AV 0x01710038). v2
lets the stock `push [ebx+0x10] / mov ecx, 0xC1BB08 (relocated by the loader) / call 0x7949E0` add the low dword
(with the carry into +0x196), then jumps at 0x73F11D and adds only the high dword into [ecx+0x196] - 0x7949E0 keeps
ecx. The object's ctor 0x73F050 has a second caller, 0x5A5D20 (unreferenced - dead code as far as a byte search
shows), which also allocates 0x18: bumped to 0x20 too, so the ctor's +0x18 store can never overrun it.

new_section.name: .expgain64
new_section.note: Two caves: the ctor copy at +0, the handler at +0x20.

code.why: ctor: high dword (payload +6) -> +0x18, then the original low-dword copy
handler: the stock call added the low dword; add the high dword, no line for 0, formatter gets (buf, low, high)

edits.why: the queued EXPGAIN object: 0x18 -> 0x20 bytes (room for the high dword at +0x18)
the ctor's other caller 0x5A5D20: 0x18 -> 0x20 bytes as well
ctor: mov eax,[ecx] opcode -> jmp rel32
handler: mov eax,[ebx+0x10] opcode (after the stock bar add) -> jmp rel32
-> its cave (the rest of mov eax,[ebx+0x10] + test eax,eax)
